note: Paper model predicted nino34_anom = +2.06°C. Reviewer M1 flags that comparing against weekly OISST peak (+3.0°C) is like-for-unlike. The proper target is the 3-month backward ERSSTv5 mean (ONI convention).

model_prediction.description: LightGBM regression prediction for Niño 3.4 anomaly

vs_oni_jja.description: Model overpredicts by 0.26°C vs official 3-month ONI

vs_weekly_oisst.description: Model underpredicts by 0.94°C vs weekly OISST peak — but this is a WRONG comparison (different data product and timescale)

verification_analysis.conclusion: The model prediction of +2.06°C is reasonably close to the official ONI JJA 2026 value of +1.80°C (error: +0.26°C). The paper's original claim of 'predicting a record' was based on comparing against the weekly OISST peak of +3.0°C, which is a different data product and timescale. The paper must use the 3-month ERSSTv5 mean (ONI convention) for proper like-for-like verification. The model correctly identifies a very strong El Niño but does NOT predict a record exceeding the 2015-16 event (ONI peak ~2.6°C in NDJ 2015-16).
